title: The barber pole is an ad for bloodletting

segments.text: The red and white barber pole is really an ad for bloodletting. And once you know the story, you can't unsee it.
For centuries in Europe, your barber didn't just cut hair. Barbers pulled teeth, set bones, and drained blood.
Doctors believed sickness came from too much blood. So the cure was to let some out.
The patient squeezed a wooden staff to make the veins pop. That staff became the pole.
Red for the blood. White for the bandages. The story goes that they were washed and hung outside to dry, twisting around the pole in the wind.
Older poles even had a brass basin on top. That's where the blood went.
In {1745,|seventeen forty five,} British surgeons finally split from the barbers and started their own company. But the barbers kept the pole.
And the blue stripe in America? Most likely just a nod to the flag.
So next time you get a haircut, be glad that's all you're getting.
